body.value: There are many important steps to take if you get a new job. It's important to have everything in order, so that you get paid on time and are not paying emergency tax.
Contact Revenue as soon as you accept the job

Give your employer your PPS number as soon as possible, so you don’t get put on emergency tax.

Register the job with Revenue in myAccount under the Jobs and Pensions section. This gets your Tax Credit Certificate (TCC) and your employer gets an RPN so the right tax is taken.

You may need to register for myAccount if you have never used it before.
Tell the Department of Social Protection that you've started work

This matters if you’re currently on (or recently on) a payment like Jobseeker’s Allowance/Benefit, One-Parent Family Payment and so on.

Close/sign off your Jobseeker’s claim when you start work (Doing this online is usually quickest).

If you can’t do it online, contact your local Intreo Centre or Social Welfare Branch Office.

If you’re not sure what else changes when you start working (secondary benefits, means tests), use the “changes that can affect your payment” guidance as your checklist.

You may be eligible for Back to Work Family Dividend if you have children and you are moving off certain payments.

If you have qualified children and you’re moving from an eligible payment into work/self-employment, check Back to Work Family Dividend and apply via DSP/MyWelfare/Intreo route.

If you’re an employee with children and under the income limits, apply for Working Family Payment online via MyWelfare.
Make sure you can access online services

A lot of Department of Social Protection services (including closing claims and some applications) rely on MyGovID or MyWelfare access:

  1. Create a basic MyGovID (email-based) if you don’t have one.
  2. If you need full access for more services, you may need a verified MyGovID, which is linked to SAFE/PSC processes.
  3. If you need a PSC/SAFE appointment, use the PSC centres list/guidance.
Update any health supports with the HSE if your income changes

When you start work your eligibility might change, but you may still qualify depending on income and circumstances:

  1. Check whether you still qualify for a medical card.
  2. If you don’t qualify for a medical card, check if you can get a GP Visit Card.
  3. If you don’t have a medical card, apply for a Drugs Payment Scheme (DPS) card.
Tell your local authority/housing supports that your income has changed

If you’re in local authority housing or receiving HAP, starting work usually means you must report income changes quickly so rent/support is recalculated:

  1. If you’re on HAP: notify your local authority about income/household changes.
  2. If you’re a local authority tenant: report income changes to your council.
  3. Find the right council contact details vis the “Find my Local Authority” tool or this list of local authorities.
